title: Bill Clinton meets Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell at a 1993 White House donors’ event
description_medium: On September 29, 1993, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell attended a White House event for donors to the restoration project and spoke with President Bill Clinton after his remarks. White House photographer Ralph Alswang documented the gathering. The photographs establish contact at the event; they do not show that Clinton knew of or participated in Epstein’s later crimes. The available account does not establish a Trump connection.
description_long: On September 29, 1993, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell attended a White House event for donors to a restoration project. Photographs taken by White House photographer Ralph Alswang show them speaking with President Bill Clinton after he delivered remarks. The gathering documents that Epstein and Maxwell had access to a presidential event and met Clinton in that setting. It predates the criminal cases that later brought Epstein’s abuse into public view. A photograph of a brief conversation does not establish what Clinton knew about Epstein or his later conduct, and it is not evidence of participation in abuse. The event described in the supplied sources concerns the Clinton White House; they do not identify Donald Trump as a participant. Its relevance is as a record of Epstein and Maxwell’s access to political and donor circles, with the limits of what a reception photograph can prove kept clear.
evidence_notes: Photographs credited to White House photographer Ralph Alswang and dated Sept. 29, 1993 by the Clinton Library show Epstein and Maxwell speaking with Clinton after donor remarks. No Trump action is part of this event.
corrected_wording: Retitled around the Clinton White House event and identified the documented participants; the former Trump framing is unsupported.

title: TrumpFile timeline alleges Mogilevich gained control of Inkombank in 1994
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline alleges that a 1994 agreement between Semion Mogilevich and Inkombank chairman Vladimir Vinogradov gave Mogilevich control of the Russian bank. The page calls Inkombank a leading Bank of New York partner, but the supplied links do not include the court documents said to support the agreement. A Guardian report on Mogilevich’s 2008 arrest does not independently verify the 1994 transaction.
description_long: The TrumpFile timeline describes an alleged 1994 agreement between Semion Mogilevich and Vladimir Vinogradov, then chairman of Inkombank, that purportedly gave Mogilevich control of the bank. It also characterizes Inkombank as a major partner of the Bank of New York. The timeline refers to court documents, but the record’s linked page does not reproduce those filings or identify a case number, court, or particular finding. The Guardian link in the packet concerns Mogilevich’s arrest in 2008 and does not report on this alleged agreement. Without the cited court record or separate reliable reporting, the terms of the agreement and whether Mogilevich took control cannot be independently established from these sources. The record also supplies no link between the alleged bank arrangement and Donald Trump. It is an allegation about Russian banking and organized-crime activity, not a substantiated Trump event. The distinction matters because allegations about financial institutions can be repeated as fact without the underlying records.
evidence_notes: The source title and synopsis allege a 1994 bank-control agreement; Guardian link addresses 2008 arrest. No underlying court file is supplied, and nothing connects the transaction to Trump.
corrected_wording: Changed the title to attribute the 1994 control claim to the timeline rather than state it as an established Trump-related event.
exact_blocker: The cited court documents are not identified or provided, so the alleged 1994 agreement, its terms, and Mogilevich’s control of Inkombank cannot be verified from the supplied sources.

title: Justice Department grant conditions for domestic-violence programs challenged and blocked
description_medium: In May 2025, the Justice Department added grant conditions that could exclude domestic-violence programs promoting diversity, equity and inclusion or transgender rights. Seventeen organizations challenged the conditions, and a federal judge temporarily blocked their use in August while the case continued. Ohio’s 2025 VAWA solicitation also warned that later federal guidance might alter or cancel awards. These developments show funding uncertainty and a legal challenge, not nationwide termination of Violence Against Women Act services.
description_long: The Violence Against Women Act supports federal grants for programs addressing domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, and related crimes. In May 2025, the Justice Department added conditions to some Office on Violence Against Women grants that would have prevented funding for programs promoting diversity, equity and inclusion or transgender rights. A coalition of 17 organizations sued, arguing the restrictions threatened established local services. On August 8, a federal judge temporarily blocked the conditions, finding the challengers were likely to succeed on claims that the rules were arbitrary and contrary to federal law; the case remained ongoing. Separately, Ohio’s 2025 VAWA solicitation invited applications while warning that later DOJ guidance could change or cancel awards. Together these sources document uncertainty and an attempted restriction on grant eligibility, followed by court intervention. They do not establish that VAWA itself was defunded nationwide or that all shelters, hotlines, legal aid, and survivor services were terminated. The record should distinguish this grant dispute from the much broader claim of program elimination.
evidence_notes: Reuters reports DOJ May grant conditions, suit by 17 groups, and Aug. 8 temporary injunction. Ohio RFP says new guidance might alter or cancel awards. No evidence of nationwide VAWA termination.
corrected_wording: Replaced categorical nationwide defunding claim with the documented DOJ grant-condition dispute and injunction.
exact_blocker: The supplied sources do not show nationwide termination or total defunding of VAWA programs; the court case over grant restrictions was ongoing in the latest cited report.

title: Trump attends a party at Moscow’s Baltschug Kempinski hotel in 1996
description_medium: During a 1996 Moscow trip, Donald Trump attended a party for American investors at the Baltschug Kempinski hotel, according to the Senate Intelligence Committee report. The committee said the gathering was arranged by businessman David Geovanis and that Trump may have begun a brief relationship with a Russian woman he met there; her name was redacted. The report does not substantiate the timeline’s claim that the hotel belonged to Semion Mogilevich.
description_long: During a November 1996 trip to Moscow, Donald Trump attended a party for a group of American investors at the Baltschug Kempinski hotel. The Senate Intelligence Committee’s report on Russian interference says Moscow-based businessman David Geovanis arranged the gathering. It describes Geovanis as a host for visiting businessmen and notes that parties and nightlife could present opportunities for Russian security services to collect information. The report says Trump may have begun a brief relationship with a Russian woman he met at the party, but her name is redacted and the account is presented as a possibility based on sources interviewed by the committee. This provides a documented context for the hotel event without establishing the timeline’s claim that Semion Mogilevich owned the property. The report does not make that ownership claim, nor does it show that the party itself was organized by Mogilevich. The event supports a record of Trump’s 1996 visit and the committee’s cautious account of a possible relationship, not the stronger title’s hotel-ownership implication.
evidence_notes: Senate report and Guardian reporting support a party for US investors at the hotel, arranged by Geovanis; report states Trump may have begun a brief relationship with a woman, identity redacted. No support for Mogilevich hotel ownership.
corrected_wording: Removed unsubstantiated Mogilevich ownership and changed title to the corroborated hotel-party event.
exact_blocker: The supplied sources do not establish that Semion Mogilevich owned the Baltschug Kempinski hotel; the possible relationship is reported cautiously and the woman's identity is redacted.

title: Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein attend an event at New York’s Duvet club
description_medium: On April 9, 1997, Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein attended a Victoria’s Secret Angels event sponsored by Rogers & Cowan at Duvet, a club on 21st Street in New York City. Getty Images identifies the men in a photograph taken by Thomas Concordia. The image documents their attendance at the same public event; it does not establish the nature of their relationship or show misconduct at the gathering.
description_long: A Getty Images photograph by Thomas Concordia records Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein at a Victoria’s Secret Angels event on April 9, 1997. The event was sponsored by Rogers & Cowan and held at Duvet, a club on 21st Street in New York City. The image caption identifies both men and gives the date and venue, supplying direct support for the event described in the timeline. The photograph is evidence that the two attended the same gathering, but it cannot by itself establish how close their relationship was, what they discussed, or whether either engaged in misconduct there. The linked Guardian article published decades later discusses photographs of Trump and Epstein from different occasions, so the Getty catalog entry is the source that pins down this specific 1997 image. Keeping the account to the documented attendance distinguishes the social event from broader claims about the men’s relationship or Epstein’s crimes.
evidence_notes: Getty catalog directly identifies the photo, date, event, sponsor, venue and photographer. Guardian covers different photos, not evidence needed for this specific image.
corrected_wording: Description now uses the direct Getty image record; preserved the appearance title while grounding it in the photographed public event.
